title: N-Queens II
statement: Return the number of distinct ways to place n non-attacking queens on an n x n board.

hints.1_question: You only need the count, not the boards. What state do you need while placing queens row by row?
hints.2_nudge: Track used columns and the two diagonals in sets (or bitmasks); count placements that reach row n.
hints.3_big_hint: bt(r): if r == n return 1; sum over safe columns c of bt(r + 1) after marking; unmark.

known_bugs.name: counts only column-safe placements (n!)
known_bugs.followup: A column-only check counts all permutations. What else must be checked?

known_bugs.name: doubles the left half (breaks for odd n)
known_bugs.followup: Mirroring only works if the first queen can't be in the middle column. What happens when n is odd?

known_bugs.name: checks every permutation of columns (O(n!) with an O(n^2) test)
known_bugs.followup: How many permutations exist for n = 10, and how many partial placements does early pruning avoid?

complexity.time: O(n!) worst case, far less with pruning
followups: How do bitmasks make each safety check O(1)?
